name: AnyDesk
description: A well-known remote-access tool built around its proprietary DeskRT codec, tuned for crisp GUI and text rendering rather than general video — with most security, admin, and collaboration features gated behind paid business and enterprise tiers.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Relies on PipeWire. Screen capture will not start without a manual confirmation from the user.

Relay Server.comment: Built on the vendor's own global distributed infrastructure. Available out of the box on cloud plans, but full traffic isolation and self-hosting your own relay inside a closed corporate network requires the top-tier Ultimate license with an On-Premises deployment.

Drawing Tablet Support.comment: Basic input works, but accurate pressure and tilt passthrough can behave incorrectly.

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: The DeskRT codec aggressively crushes quality and color depth, so when the network dips, on-screen text turns into unreadable pixel mush.

H.264 Codec.comment: Replaced by the proprietary DeskRT algorithm.

AV1 Codec.comment: Not used. AnyDesk relies on its proprietary DeskRT codec, purpose-built for transmitting GUIs (windows, text) rather than general video.

Session Sharing.comment: On the free version, parallel connections are quickly flagged as commercial activity and blocked.

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Supported in Enterprise configurations for terminal servers (Windows Server), but requires a specialized license.

Virtual Display.comment: There is no native built-in virtual display driver; users working with headless servers have to resort to third-party workarounds.

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: Thanks to the proprietary DeskRT codec, it reliably holds a true 60 FPS in normal scenarios and gracefully drops frames when the network dips, but is architecturally capped at 60 FPS.

Session Recording.comment: Session recording is blocked for free users and requires a commercial subscription.

Pre-Login Access.comment: The service starts before login, but the reliability of unattended access on the free version depends on the detection algorithms.

No Account Required.comment: Like TeamViewer, the service has become aggressive about blocking connections without an account, citing suspected 'commercial use.'

SSO / OIDC.comment: Corporate Single Sign-On integration is only available on the Advanced and Enterprise plans.

2FA / MFA.comment: 2FA can be set up for free on a specific workstation, but global policies require payment.

Address Book.comment: The ability to create shared team address books is strictly tied to the license tier.

Audit Logs.comment: REST API access and detailed session logs are only available on the more expensive subscriptions.

Mass Deployment.comment: Generating a custom client (AnyDesk Custom Client) with policies for silent deployment is a paid feature.

RBAC.comment: Advanced role management in the my.anydesk console is only available to enterprise customers.

Privacy Mode (Black Screen).comment: Screen Privacy mode requires installing a display driver and holding a paid license.

Remote Printing.comment: Works via the virtual AnyDesk Printer driver; the feature is locked on the free version.

Generic USB Passthrough.comment: Limited support (mainly smart card and simple USB dongle passthrough via TCP tunneling).

File Manager UI.comment: A separate file transfer mode is available.

On-Screen Whiteboard.comment: A built-in Whiteboard drawing tool is available over the streamed screen.

Proxy Support.comment: Native support for HTTP, SOCKS5, and NTLM proxies.

UAC Handling.comment: Requires the app to be pre-installed as a system service. In portable (non-installed) mode, SYSTEM privileges are not used.

Self-hosted.comment: AnyDesk On-Premises exists as an isolated network appliance server, but it is very expensive and only sold on the Enterprise plan.

Browser client.comment: A web client is available at go.anydesk.com.

Headless mode.comment: Sometimes requires installing a virtual display driver (built into the client) or a hardware monitor emulator.

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Screen streaming works via PipeWire/XDG portals, but input control (mouse and keyboard emulation) often drops out or behaves unreliably.

Android: Host.comment: Full remote control (not just screen viewing) requires installing an additional, phone-vendor-specific AnyDesk Control Plugin from Google Play.

Web Browser: Client.comment: Available via the go.anydesk.com portal (runs on WebAssembly).

Free Tier.comment: Strictly non-commercial use only. There are session-time limits and aggressive connection blocking at the slightest suspicion of work-related use.

Personal: Monthly.comment: Solo plan (1 licensed user, 1 simultaneous outgoing connection). Billing requires paying 100% upfront for the full year.

Team / Business: Monthly.comment: Standard plan. Adds basic user management (up to 20 accounts), but only includes 1 parallel connection channel by default.

Enterprise.comment: Advanced plan. Includes mass deployment tools (MSI) and session auditing. True isolated On-Premises deployment (your own AnyDesk server) costs significantly more and is only sold on request.
